valid.name: MemberExpression property access literally named 'arguments' - not flagged (object literal key declarations are still flagged separately, since only the MemberExpression-property read is excluded)
eval("arguments.length") - not flagged; arguments identifier is inside a string literal, invisible to static AST analysis (known, permanent limitation)

fn.arguments deprecated accessor - not flagged; no reliable static signal distinguishes a function's deprecated .arguments accessor from a legitimate data property literally named 'arguments' (documented known limitation)

invalid.name: bare arguments identifier inside a function - flagged

invalid.code: function fn() { const args = arguments; return args; }
invalid.name: arguments assigned to a variable - flagged

object literal Property key literally named 'arguments' - flagged; the selector only excludes MemberExpression-property reads, not ObjectExpression Property keys (documents the actual boundary of the exclusion)
